recipes.name: Braised Pork Roast with Butternut Squash

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Season pork loin with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-proof skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown pork loin on all sides in the hot oil, about 10 minutes total. Remove pork loin from the pan, and set aside. Pour in white wine, and bring to a simmer, stirring to dissolve caramelized bits in the pan.

Scatter butternut squash and onion in the skillet and place the browned pork loin on top so they work as a roasting rack. Stir applesauce, mustard, soy sauce, sugar, and cinnamon together in a bowl. Pour over pork loin, then cover the pan with a lid or a double layer of aluminum foil.
Bake pork loin in preheated oven until it has reached an internal temperature of 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 1 hour. Allow to rest for 10 minutes before serving

raw_recipe.headline: Braised Pork Roast with Butternut Squash
raw_recipe.description: A pork roast braises with onions and butternut squash in a sweet and savory applesauce-mustard sauce for a comforting fall dinner.

review.reviewBody: How delicious was this? Outstanding! I prepared exactly as written, but added some sliced granny smith apple and dried cranberries to the vegetable mix, and decreased the brown sugar to 1/4 cup. Roasted for about 1 hr 10 minutes, and let the meat rest before carving. Tender, flavorful, sweet, it was perfect. The house smelled wonderful while this was cooking. Thanks for sharing this terrific recipe, SJRJA, it's going to be a classic in this house.

Absolutely wonderful! Roast was 6.5 lbs. Squash resulted in over 4 C of cubes. Used a small lunch single applesauce and 2 Pippin apples in SMALL cubes...Cinnamon and the sugar. Basically, followed the recipe and method in a 3.5 qt. LeCrueset Casserole Pot....this meal fed 2 of us over a week. Near end I separated items serving fresh boiled Spinach and and mixed a cooked medium sweet potato with the left juice and squash...then mashed....Oh my! Really good meal(s)!!!

Wow! This was really tasty! Must admit, I didn't think it would be as I was making it but after the favors blended - Wow! I did make several changes but the flavor, I think, would basically be the same. I followed all of step 1 but I only had Moscato so used that instead of dry white wine. I added only 1/2 an onion and 2 cut up apples (didn't have applesauce either) to the juice in the pan. Didn't have squash so omitted that. Mixed up all the other ingredients and added the mixture to the pan and simmered for a bit. Then, since I wanted to use my crock pot, I put 1/2 the mixture from the pan in my crock, put the browned roast in, then the rest of the mixture! Left it on high for about 4+ hours and it was fall apart tender so tasty! Will definitely make this again!

I added two chopped apples with the squash and onion and in the interest of calorie counting, cut the sugar down to one Tablespoon which was perfect. I also used apple cider in place of sauce (because it's what I had on hand) and added an extra cup of water so I could slow cook it. Cooked at 250 for four hours, and it was fork tender and delicious. To not kill our diets I served it with fresh steamed green beans and husband loved it in spite of presence of veggies. It's a keeper!

I used 1/4 cup brown sugar and added two Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced to the vegetables. Divided the sauce mixture and slathered about half of it on the roast prior to roasting. About halfway through, slathered the other half of the sauce on the pork. Scattered ½ cup of dried cranberries on the vegetables. While pork rested, tented in foil, I spooned the vegetables out of the Dutch oven, using a slotted spoon. Simmered the sauce until it started to thicken just a bit. Poured sauce over vegetables and served with the pork. I will make again. It's good....really good.

This was really good. As many reviewers suggested I didn't add any sugar. I was using yams instead of butternut squash and they're so sweet plus the applesauce was already sweet that I didn't see the need for any sugar. I also added a half pound of bacon but I won't do that again just because it was a waste, we couldn't taste it at all.

I did it in my cast iron dutch oven and baked it at 300 for 1 1/2 hrs. It was tender and juicy! The yams and onion were also done to perfection. We love yams and I am always looking for savory dishes to use them in. They really don't need all the sugar and marshmallows that recipes want you to put on them all the time. Perfect with pork!
I left out the brown sugar and cinnamon because it sounded way too sweet. After browning the roast, I put it all in the oven, covered, at 225, for about 6 hours. It's pretty fantastic.

Love this one, and though I can't manage to follow the recipe exactly, it always turns out great. I put in extra squash, and after the first meal use the squash, onions and dripping to make a butternut squash soup. I add vegetable broth and puree it, add seasoning if needed and bam! soup for lunch.

I had a pork tenderloin to use up and this recipe sounded so good. I obviously didn't need an hour of roasting time, so I made sure the squash was cut into smaller chunks and 45 minutes later it was done to perfection. it was wonderful, raves around the table. Will make again! Thanks.

This is easy and fantastic! Whole family loved it. I would suggest making your own apple sauce for this vs store bought...makes a HUGE difference in flavor (just slice up a couple Granny Smiths, put in sauce pot with 1/4 c water and a tsp white or brown sugar; bring to boil and simmer 15 min or til tender, mash up a bit). I've made it as is, and I've varied it as well by adding carrots and sweet potato...I've also added a Tbsp of cider vinegar on occasion...comes out great every time!

I liked this recipe: it was fun to make, pretty quick process. I did not have butternut and also a Dutch pan or similar, so I was modding a lot. I nestled pork on some red onions I grew. Substituted sesame oil for soy sauce, honey for the sugar. It turned out pretty moist and sweet. Checked all the boxes for me. Very pleased, Okay out wasn't dish of the year but we enjoyed it
Delicioso!!
Yummy Yummy Yummy Yummy Yummy Yummy Yummy Yummy
Easy instructions I ommited the applesauce since I didn't have any.

So the flavor was great!!! I added carrots, because a) I had some, and b) some other reviewer suggested them. Note: cut thin. 
Next time I will probably use another reviewers suggestion: shoulder roast. Loin is just so easily dry.

I used this recipe as a base and modified for what I had on hand. i didn't have applesauce...cooked and chopped fresh apple, added a couple of dates that were left. Upped the veggies: fresh beets, squash, sweet potatoes, and onions. IT WAS OUTSTANDING! I want to use parsnips and turnips with the squash next time. Can't wait to make this again.

I made this as written in my LeCruset. Unlike other reviewers, I found the pork dry, pink in the middle, and the squash was overcooked, almost to mush. I wonder if the temp got too hot inside the cast iron pan. It may be easy but I won’t be making it again.

Scrumptious! I probably didn’t cook it long enough. The pork was a little tough, but when I reheated it the next day, it was perfect. I was nervous about peeling the squash. I popped it in the microwave, whole, for a 1 minute and it was very easy to peel with a vegetable peeler. Definitely will make again.
This is the best pork roast ever! I followed the recipe exactly except doubled it. I also added dried cranberries. Loved it!
